text: Languor [Lat. languere , to be faint, languish]: Ger. Schlaffheit ; Fr. langueur ; Ital. languore . A listless unwillingness to exert oneself; a form of depression or lack of tone (atonia), with sensations of fatigue, feebleness, or faintness. It is a frequent symptom in depleted conditions of body and mind, in convalescence, &c. It also represents a temperamental characteristic; and as a temporary symptom is perfectly normal and usual. Atmospheric and temperature conditions frequently induce the state of languor, as in what is called 'spring fever.' ( J.J. ) Footnote [
